problem: Existing VLN models rely on simple data augmentation or expansion and fail to exploit the intrinsic relationship between the instruction and visual/trajectory modalities.
motivation: Fusing multiple modalities is central to VLN, and the instruction's key information (entities, directions) should be explicitly matched with what the agent sees and how it moves to provide feedback for self-tuning.
key_idea: VIM-Net adds two matching feedback modules, one matching visual recognition targets with instruction entities and one matching trajectory features with instruction movement directions, to self-tune the navigation policy.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation details can be cited. The abstract claims that explicit matching of vital instruction information (entities and directions) with perception and trajectory is more effective than plain data augmentation.
method: V-mat (visual matching feedback module): matches the target information from visual recognition with entity information extracted from the command.
T-mat (trajectory matching feedback module): matches the serialized trajectory feature with the movement direction described in the command.
VIM-Net: a feedback self-tuning network built from V-mat and T-mat, trained and evaluated on R2R in the Matterport3D simulator.

setting.backbone: VIM-Net (trained neural network with V-mat and T-mat modules; details not in abstract)
setting.training_data: R2R training data (details not given in abstract)
setting.observation: panoramic RGB in Matterport3D simulator (assumed; not stated in abstract)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (assumed for Matterport3D simulator)

limitations: Abstract gives no quantitative results, so the size of the gain cannot be assessed.
